recipes.name: Sesame Shrimp Stir-Fry
ingredients_raw: 1 pound medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
1 red bell pepper, sliced into thin strips

steps.text: In a medium saucepan, bring salted water to a boil. Add rice, reduce heat, cover and simmer for 20 minutes.
While rice is simmering, combine shrimp, ginger, cayenne pepper, garlic, sesame seeds and black pepper in a large plastic food storage bag. Allow to marinate in the refrigerator.

Heat sesame oil in a large wok or skillet. Add red bell pepper and green onions; saute 3 to 4 minutes to soften slightly Add teriyaki sauce. Add peas and shrimp with seasoning; saute 4 minutes or until shrimp are opaque.
Stir cornstarch into chicken broth and add to wok; cook, stirring until mixture boils. Sprinkle with salt. Spoon shrimp mixture over rice.

raw_recipe.headline: Sesame Shrimp Stir-Fry
raw_recipe.description: This quick and tasty main dish has a double hit of sesame oil and seeds that add nutty flavor to crisp peppers and shrimp.

review.reviewBody: Can I give this 10 stars?? Excellent dish! Couple changes I made.. I used fresh grated ginger instead of powdered and added some lemon zest to the shrimp. I used 8-12 shrimp per pound then partial way through I butterflied them in half. The larger shrimp the better you are, these things are as succulant as lobster tails!! A+++ recipe, great reviews from guests! Thanks for adding it :)

I admit that I use recipes as a base and make lots of changes. I didn't have cayanne pepper so I used lots of red pepper flakes. I had 3 lbs of shrimp so I didn't measure out the spices for the marinade just kept adding until the shrimp were coated. With the juices from the shrimp and veggies I didn't add the chicken broth. I had a bottle of Sesame teriyaki sauce so used that and added corn starch at the end to thicken up the sauce. Topped off at the end with Sesame oil instead of using that for cooing. It had a great spice to it without being too spicy.

Loved this! I bought fresh spot prawns, which are in season here.. They are delicious on their own. Used hoisin sauce instead of teriyaki and mixed it with the chicken broth and cornstarch. Used canola oil to cook and seasoned with 1/2 tsp of sesame oil at the end. I did everything else as the recipe. I will make this again. delicious..but a little messy as we used our fingers to remove the shells.

This was really tasty. My husband was raving. I added onion (caramelized) and mushrooms to the vegetable saute. I also used green beans (blanched) instead of snow peas because that's what I had. Everything else was exactly to the recipe. Will definitely make this again.

Great recipe! I made some changes based on personal preference. I toasted the sesame seeds, adds more flavor (my opinion). I did saute the vegetables & shrimp in sesame oil. If you keep it on medium heat, it won't burn. Some reviews said it burns. (???) I used a package of frozen stir fry vegetables. Everything came out wonderful! A keeper.

This turned out great! Used carrots, celery, mushrooms, onions, and red pepper. Rubbed the garlic mixture onto the shrimp without using a bag. Only thing I’d change next time is the amount of cayenne...my kids found it to be a bit spicy. Everyone enjoyed it though!

I noted to put less cayenne in. It was a little strong on heat. Other than that, it was a great tasting meal that was filling. I am putting in 1/8th tsp cayenne instead of 1/4 tsp. I granted fresh ginger also.

I didn't cook the vegies with the sesame oil, as someone pointed out, it would have way too strong. I added about a tablespoon to the shrimp mixture in the bag and the same to the sauce. we loved it. Practically liked the pan.

Delicious! My wife and daughter loved it! Alterations I made: Added yellow and orange bell pepper, as well as the red, keep the appropriate proportions. My wife doesn't care for snap peas, so I substituted green beans and it worked out great. I added a little more teriyaki sauce, maybe 2 or 3 Tablespoons more, and serve it with noodles instead of rice.
Used peanut oil to sauté but sesame oil later. Also used hoisin sauce. Very good and fast to come together.

We liked it. Quick and easy. I didn't have the peas, so I substituted broccoli and shredded cabbage -- the more veggies the better! Cabbage has a very subtle flavor, and is overpowered by most other things, so it's great in a recipe like this; it adds some texture and crunch, and also healthy fiber, while going unnoticed by people who think they "don't like cabbage!" I would add a bit extra teriyaki or soy sauce, too.
Very good! Lots of flavor! I omitted the red pepper and did broccoli instead. I also doubled the sauce. Turned out perfect. Would make again

I followed the recipe exactly... but I made a few changes. How many reviewers start off with that?! So I did not follow the recipe exactly, and you can take this review for what it's worth as a result. I did follow it pretty closely though. What I made I and my family liked! I didn't have sesame seeds. I used chicken bullion instead of broth. I added half a red and half an orange bell pepper, a can of water chestnuts and "julliended" a couple of carrots. The flavors blended nicely. The shrimp tasted great and the sauce had just the right amount of heat and wasn't soupy or like gravy either. Thanks for the recipe Debbie! :-)

Excellent recipe & easy to modify to the ingredients you have on hand. I used garlic scapes, grated frozen ginger and fresh green onion. I used half of the black & cayenne pepper and it was still plenty. The only thing I might change is to not use as much corn starch, as it tightens up quickly.
Awesome recipe. I didn’t change much. No terryaki so I used hoisin instead….hands down, the best!
My husband and I both loved this recipe. The only change I made was using sushi-style pickled ginger instead of dried because that is what I had on hand. Will definitely make again.

I made this last evening for supper. Pretty much followed the recipe except I used a 12 ounce package of thawed Sugar snap peas, sliced red and yellow peppers, and green beans, with a small amount of leftover chopped jarred pimentos. Was good, but if I make this again, I'll add more teriyaki sauce and chicken broth. A little too light on flavor and moisture for my taste, but worth making again. Got 4 one cup servings out of recipe.
Very easy and I received rave reviews!!
Very good! Ginger was great with it!
